study.title: Graded brain fMRI response to somatic and visual acupuncture stimulation
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover fMRI experiment with six experimental conditions (three dose levels × two acupuncture modalities)
study.inclusion_criteria: No contraindications against an MRI examination and no history of a neurological disorder; all participants were right-handed and had no visual deficits
study.exclusion_criteria: Contraindications against MRI examination; history of neurological disorder; visual deficits; not right-handed

neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian filter kernel at full-width-half-maximum of 8 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: six directional movement parameters used as nuisance regressor to correct head motion; foam padding used to minimize head movement
statistical_thresholds_exact: GLM: false discovery rate (FDR) correction of q < 0.05 applied to the voxel level for the whole brain

extraction_notes.note: The paper references Supplementary Table 1 containing full coordinate tables for brain regions evoked by different doses of SA and VA, and Supplementary Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 1 showing the difference map between the two acupuncture modalities. These supplementary materials were not provided in the PDF. Therefore, no MNI coordinates for any of the GLM contrast results could be extracted; all coordinate fields for GLM results are marked as null/not_reported.

All GLM brain activation results (Fig. 3A, 3B, 3C, 3D) are shown as brain images with T-value color scales but without a coordinate table in the main text. The full coordinate tables are only in supplements not provided.

MVPA searchlight results (Fig. 4A, 4B) show spatial maps of classification accuracy on brain images. No coordinate tables are provided in the main text or figure captions; brain region names only were extracted from text descriptions.

The study uses a within-subject design where all 24 participants experienced all 6 conditions (SA and VA at three dose levels). The 'arms' of SA and VA are therefore conditions within the same participants, not independent participant groups. The arm structure was preserved to facilitate contrast extraction but reviewers should note this is a within-subject crossover design.

The paper states fMRI runs had 37 slices (functional), TR = 2000 ms, but also states the high-pass filter was 128 Hz. This appears to be a reporting convention (high-pass filter cutoff of 128 s, not 128 Hz). Transcribed exactly as written in the paper.
Adverse events are not discussed in the paper. No safety/tolerability section was found.

Blinding of participants was not formally assessed. Participants in VA conditions were not blinded in the traditional sense — they knew they were watching a video. No formal blinding success assessment or allocation guessing measure was reported.

Expectancy and credibility were not formally measured using validated instruments such as the Credibility-Expectancy Questionnaire. Only the MASS (deqi sensation) and a simple anxiety scale were reported.

The training session used a needle of 40 mm length, 0.25 mm diameter (WooJeon Acupuncture), while the fMRI session used a nonmagnetic titanium needle of 40 mm length, 0.20 mm diameter (DongBang Acupuncture). These are different needles for training vs. scanning.

The paper states anxiety was evaluated 'both before and after receiving the acupuncture treatment' but only the pre-acupuncture value (−1.58 ± 0.47) appears in Table 1. Post-acupuncture anxiety values are not reported in the main text.

The MVPA analyses were conducted with AFNI (version 21.3.07) for preprocessing and Python (Nilearn and scikit-learn) for classification, which is separate from the GLM preprocessing pipeline (SPM12). Both pipelines were used within the same study but on independent analyses.

The paper states 'No brain regions decreased significantly in either contrast' for SA stimulation effect, SA dose effect, VA stimulation effect, and VA dose effect. This refers to deactivation relative to baseline/lower dose; the paper explicitly states no significant decreases.
